title: Embarrassing concentration problems every time I watch a film

commenti.body:
Go to the cinema. 

It’s a different experience watching films at home because you can “multitask”

If you absolutely can’t go to the cinema then put your phone in another room. Set the lighting low. Make it a distinct event as opposed to watching tv. 


Don’t beat yourself up about it. You don’t have to like/engage with everything you watch. Seek out films that do speak to you.

> Don’t beat yourself up about it. You don’t have to like/engage with everything you watch.

this is correct, don't feel pressured to enjoy things OP

I think a lot of people lose focus with artsy films because they are mostly thinking about the plot while they are watching. A movie like Wings of desire is quickly going to lose your interest if the actual story is all you are watching for. 

Instead in the “boring” scenes try asking yourself why the camera is positioned the way it is, why do they cut where they do, what is the sound editing try to convey, etc. There are a million different cinematic techniques at play in any given shot, especially when it is by a master director such as Wim Wenders. 

Also Wings of desire is a very slow and dull movie even for seasoned art house fans so don’t feel bad about losing focus during that one. Maybe try something like The earrings of Madame De… and see if you enjoy an art film with a little more plot substance.

Honestly I kinda feel you there, I have bad ADHD and it gets awful when watching some movies. 

I’ve gotten back into watching films almost every day again before bed by doing something that I’m sure most here would not approve of. I lay in bed (where I’d be anyways when watching), but keep my laptop open while following with the movie. 

Sometimes it might get a little boring or slow and I might check Twitter or something like that for a sec then get reeled back in. That being said, I make sure not to miss any dialogue, and will rewind 10-20 seconds if I miss anything. 

While doing this I’m also able to look up things related to the film I’m watching, like check out a historical reference that went over my head for instance, or by having the Wikipedia page open to scan in case I missed something (making sure not to read ahead in the plot though, which doesn’t always work out in my favor.)

Since I’m laying on my side usually, my TV is in perfect view above where my laptop screen is, allowing some buffer room of course. So if I miss a piece of dialogue on the TV, I’ll see the subtitles shown and rewind a bit and make sure to focus my attention solely on the film so I don’t miss important events. 

I also use my laptop to take any notes about the film for later so I can review better for my website. It’s not a big site or anything, just my personal blog, but I like writing and movies and have been trying to get better at reviewing.

Of course, there are many movies where I don’t do this at all. If I’m gripped by a movie, I’ll just watch it normally. I’ve also been going to the theater more often very recently after buying an AMC A-List pass a couple weeks back. There’s basically no way for me to not be into the film if I’m seated at a theater with surround sound and a massive screen lol.

First question, have you ever been tested for ADHD or some other cognitive issue?  That’s not always the reason but it certainly can help.

As someone whose attention has definitely faded over the years, the biggest thing I’ve found that helps is to *just* watch.  I remove distractions like my phone and force myself to focus for at least like 15 minutes. I don’t check the duration, I don’t pause to check something, I just watch.  It doesn’t always work (I’ve been watching *the headless woman* in 30 minute chunks because I keep getting distracted) but if I have nothing to do but watch the movie then I focus more, and the more I focus the more I want to keep watching if the movie is good.  Arthouse cinema in particular rewards a focused viewer since there tends to be more subtlety and nuance (especially visually) and I think that kind of creates a cycle.  If you’re not paying full attention at the start then you miss the sorts of things that will make you want to pay even more attention later and you get taken out… but if you just watch, and the movie vibes with you then you’ll hopefully become *even more* engaged.

It’s something I struggle with too, but I’ve definitely found forcing myself to watch tends to help.
